summary: @ornikar/jest-config-react preinstall drops Bun runtime to execute obfuscated sibling payload
details: The package's preinstall script (setup.mjs) is itself obfuscated (obfuscator.io-style identifier mangling and per-call proxy objects wrapping ordinary Node stdlib calls such as https.get, fs.writeFileSync, execFileSync, and an ldd/os-release probe for musl/Alpine). On npm install it fetches the Bun runtime from https://github.com/oven-sh/bun/releases/download/bun-v1.3.13/<bun-*.zip> into a temporary directory, chmods it executable, and invokes it against the sibling file math_init.js via execFileSync. math_init.js is a 727KB heavily obfuscated bundle (string-array rotation over ~1000 literals, mangled identifiers) whose name is unrelated to its content. A jest configuration package has no legitimate need to fetch a second language runtime at install time and use it to execute a bundled obfuscated payload; the alternate-runtime dispatch bypasses Node-scoped install-time scanning, and the obfuscation of both the loader and the payload is intended to defeat inspection of what actually runs on each installer machine.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
